messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Modifying themes
parts:
Hi all -

Some updates on the theme system

I've implemented the + operator for themes:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/573/files#diff-9

Now you can do things like:
  theme_bw() + opts(axis.title.x = element_text(colour='red'))

I've also updated theme_bw() to use it:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/573/files#diff-12


The next steps are to deal with theme_update and update_element. I've always found it kind of confusing to work with them. Here are some changes that I think would be beneficial:

* Get rid of theme_update and update_element.
* Add an operator like %|%, which can be used to update individual properties of elements. For example:
  mytheme <- theme_bw()
  mytheme <- mytheme | opts(text = element_text(colour="red"))

One consequence of removing update_theme and update_element is that the current theme can't be modified in place. You'd have to do something like the above, and then:
  theme_set(mytheme)

Thoughts? I'm not sure if these changes should go in 0.9.2 because they'll break some functionality. But I suspect that people don't use theme_update and update_element very often anyway.

-Winston

Hi all -

Some updates on the theme system

I've implemented the + operator for themes:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/573/files#diff-9

Now you can do things like:
  theme_bw() + opts(axis.title.x = element_text(colour='red'))

I've also updated theme_bw() to use it:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/573/files#diff-12


The next steps are to deal with theme_update and update_element. I've always found it kind of confusing to work with them. Here are some changes that I think would be beneficial:

* Get rid of theme_update and update_element.
* Add an operator like %|%, which can be used to update individual properties of elements. For example:
  mytheme <- theme_bw()
  mytheme <- mytheme | opts(text = element_text(colour="red"))

One consequence of removing update_theme and update_element is that the current theme can't be modified in place. You'd have to do something like the above, and then:
  theme_set(mytheme)

Thoughts? I'm not sure if these changes should go in 0.9.2 because they'll break some functionality. But I suspect that people don't use theme_update and update_element very often anyway.

I went ahead and implemented a | operator for modifying element properties. Now you can do this to modify specified properties of theme elements:
  mytheme <- theme_bw() | opts(text=element_text(colour='red'))
  qplot(1:3, 1:3) + mytheme

Notice that this is different from using +, which replaces the whole element. For example, this won't work because text properties like size, family, etc, are NULL:
  mytheme <- theme_bw() + opts(text=element_text(colour='red'))
  qplot(1:3, 1:3) + mytheme


So far, so good. But the syntax for adding to a ggplot object (not yet implemented) would look a little weird. For example:
  qplot(1:3, 1:3) | opts(text=element_text(colour='red'))


One possible solution is, instead of using things like this:
  mytheme | opts(...)
  qplot(...) | opts(...)
it could be implemented by adding a new function, modopts():
  mytheme + modopts(...)
  qplot(...) + modopts(...)


Thoughts?

-Winston

On 2012-Jun-05, at 23:36 , Winston Chang wrote:
>
>> I've implemented the + operator for themes:
>> https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/573/files#diff-9

>> Thoughts? I'm not sure if these changes should go in 0.9.2 because they'll break some functionality. But I suspect that people don't use theme_update and update_element very often anyway.
>
> I went ahead and implemented a | operator for modifying element properties. Now you can do this to modify specified properties of theme elements:
> mytheme <- theme_bw() | opts(text=element_text(colour='red'))
> qplot(1:3, 1:3) + mytheme
>
> Notice that this is different from using +, which replaces the whole element. For example, this won't work because text properties like size, family, etc, are NULL:
> mytheme <- theme_bw() + opts(text=element_text(colour='red'))
> qplot(1:3, 1:3) + mytheme

The + operator is great. It's very natural in ggplot's syntax, congrats.

But, like Brian, I'm not sure I understand the point of the %|% operator and even if it is what I think it is (replace just one element of a base property), I don't think it should exist as such, I think it should just work with + (easy to say, probably less to implement but well, you asked for feedback ;) )

The key is probably to be able to use element_*** on a base property of the theme (e.g. element_text on text) *without specifying everything*. Maybe all the base properties should exist outside of any theme or in the theme function arguments, so that it is always possible to fall back on them?


Also, in Brian's example:

opts(text = element_text(... something appropriate ...),
axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8), angle=45),
axis.text.x = element_text(colour="green"),
axis.text.y = element_text(colour="red", angle=90))
+ opts(axis.text.y = element_text(colour="purple"))

I think the y axis text should be 0.8 times the base size, at 90º and purple, i.e. each modification should be incremental.

In your implementation of + for themes you write:
# Can't use modifyList here since it works recursively and drops NULLs
I think this is exactly what + should do though: modify the appropriate list element, dropping NULLs (alternatively the element_*** functions could only return non NULL items but that would probably be more cumbersome to implement). The sequence of modifications in the example above should be equivalent to doing:

mytheme$axis.text$size = rel(0.8)
mytheme$axis.text$angle = 45
mytheme$axis.text.x$colour = "green"
mytheme$axis.text.y$colour = "red"
mytheme$axis.text.y$angle = 90
mytheme$axis.text.y$colour = "purple"

and only this.


Ideally, I would advocate for this:
- the theme is a list of lists, with either
. only the defined properties at each level (that would be cleaner to display)
. or NULL for undefined properties at each level (this is probably easier to implement and work with)
- each element of the list can be modified independently, including the base elements, using the usual $ syntax
- the element_*** functions just allow to make those same modifications through functions, which help checking that the arguments are correct (it's not done at the moment though, but I guess this was the appeal of using functions, otherwise $ really seems more practical)
- the + operator works with lists of objects of class "element" (opts() calls basically) and can be used with ggplots
ggplot(...) + geom_***(...) + opts(axis.text=element_text(...))
or themes
theme_grey(...) + opts(axis.text=element_text(...))

What do you guys think?

PS: additional questions : besides theme elements, what can opts be used for? I see title but that's about it. If that's the case maybe another name would be more appropriate.

Jean-Olivier Irisson

wanted to explicitly force an element to inherit a property from its

parts: > What do you have in mind for items that are not set and not inherited? What to do with them?
Those should be errors.

> Maybe there's the distinction between drawing something an not drawing anything. But this could be signified by using
>
>        mytheme$axis.text.x = NULL
>
> to not draw the x axis title. Or
>
>        mytheme$axis = NULL
>
> to no draw any axis at all. I.e. the element itself is NULL, not a list of NULLs. Inheritance from this should work because extracting something (with $) from NULL returns NULL.
>
> Or maybe NULL can mean "do not draw" and NA can mean "no instruction available, just inherit".

You need to distinguish between

element_text(colour = NULL)

and

element_text()

which both produce the same output - i.e. you need to distinguish
between saying that the element should inherit from its parent, vs
stay unchanged. I think the clearest behaviour (in line with how
scales work) is for:

+ element_text(colour = NULL)

to leave the colour unchanged and

+ element_text(colour = inherit())

to force colour to be inherited from the parent.

One other thing we'd need to make clear is that

+ element_text(size = rel(0.8)) + element_text(size = rel(0.5))

gives a text size of 0.5 relative to it's parent, not 0.8 * 0.5 = 0.4.

Hadley

Here are some examples to illustrate how it all works. First, note that there's the elements in the theme object may have NULL properties -- if you access them directly, you'll see that the (non-root) elements are like this. The calc_element function figures out the properties with inheritance.

mytheme <-theme_grey() + 
  opts(

axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8), angle=45),
    axis.text.x = element_text(colour="green"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour="red", angle=90))

mytheme$text

#  $ family    : chr "Helvetica"
#  $ face      : chr "plain"
#  $ colour    : chr "black"
#  $ size      : num 12
#  $ hjust     : num 0.5
#  $ vjust     : num 0.5
#  $ angle     : num 0
#  $ lineheight: num 0.9
#  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

mytheme$axis.text
# List of 8
#  $ family    : NULL
#  $ face      : NULL
#  $ colour    : NULL
#  $ size      :Class 'rel'  num 0.8
#  $ hjust     : NULL
#  $ vjust     : NULL
#  $ angle     : num 45
#  $ lineheight: NULL
#  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

mytheme$axis.text.y
# List of 8
#  $ family    : NULL
#  $ face      : NULL
#  $ colour    : chr "red"
#  $ size      : NULL

#  $ lineheight: num 0.9

#  $ family    : chr "Helvetica"
#  $ face      : chr "plain"
#  $ colour    : chr "black"

#  $ vjust     : num 0.5

#  $ lineheight: num 0.9

#  $ face      : chr "plain"
#  $ colour    : chr "red"
#  $ size      : num 9.6

#  $ vjust     : num 0.5
#  $ angle     : num 90
#  $ lineheight: num 0.9
#  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"




The issue with the + operator is that it replaces the element entirely. Suppose I want to change my base 'text' element so that it is red. If I don't define all the element properties, I get a bunch of NULLs, which is a problem for a root node:

mytheme <- theme_grey() + opts(text = element_text(colour='red'))
mytheme$text
# List of 8
#  $ family    : NULL
#  $ face      : NULL
#  $ colour    : chr "red"
#  $ size      : NULL
#  $ hjust     : NULL
#  $ vjust     : NULL
#  $ angle     : NULL
#  $ lineheight: NULL
#  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

# calc_element throws an error in this case
calc_element("text", mytheme)
# Error in calc_element("text", mytheme) : 
#   Theme element text has NULL property: family, face, size, hjust, vjust, angle, lineheight


The purpose of the | operator is to change just a single property, without throwing out all the others. For example:

mytheme <- theme_grey() | opts(text = element_text(colour='red'))
mytheme$text
# List of 8
#  $ family    : chr "Helvetica"
#  $ face      : chr "plain"
#  $ colour    : chr "red"
#  $ size      : num 12
#  $ hjust     : num 0.5
#  $ vjust     : num 0.5
#  $ angle     : num 0
#  $ lineheight: num 0.9
#  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"


It can also be used on non-root elements to change a single property. For example, in theme_grey, 'axis.text' is defined as:
    axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8), colour = "grey50")

To change just the color (and not the size), you could do:
   mytheme <- theme_grey() | opts(axis.text = element_text(colour="red"))


I can see how this syntax could be confusing, though.

Using J-O and Hadley's suggestions, the + operator would behave like the | operator presently does, except that there would be an inherit() value that specifically means to inherit this from the parent.

In general I think this makes sense, but it could potentially break exisiting code since it changes the behavior of the + operator.


-Winston

parts:
After some discussion with Hadley, here's what I ended up doing. The + operator replaces a specific properties of elements. There's also a %+replace% operator, which replaces the entire element. This operator probably will not see much use, except by someone who is creating a theme. See the definition of theme_bw() for an example: https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/pull/573/files#L22R67



> mytheme <- theme_grey() + theme(text = element_text(colour='red'))
> mytheme$text
List of 8
 $ family    : chr "Helvetica"
 $ face      : chr "plain"
 $ colour    : chr "red"
 $ size      : num 12
 $ hjust     : num 0.5
 $ vjust     : num 0.5
 $ angle     : num 0
 $ lineheight: num 0.9
- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

> mytheme <- theme_grey() %+replace% theme(text = element_text(colour='red'))
> mytheme$text
List of 8
 $ family    : NULL
 $ face      : NULL
 $ colour    : chr "red"
 $ size      : NULL
 $ hjust     : NULL
 $ vjust     : NULL
 $ angle     : NULL
 $ lineheight: NULL
- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

There are a lot of changes under the hood (72 commits!). It's kind of a miracle that everything still seems to work -- there's absolutely no way this revamp would have been possible without a solid testing system.

Here are some of the more visible changes that weren't previously mentioned:
* opts() is now deprecated, in favor of theme().
* opts(title='mytitle') is now deprecated. Instead use labs(title='mytitle'), or ggtitle('mytitle').
* theme_update() and update_element() are deprecated.

Good question... I'm not totally sure, but I think the % signs just indicate that it's an infix operator. There are built-in operators (+, *, /, etc) that don't require the % signs around them.

More to the point: I'm still confused about whether NULL indicates "this property inherits from above" or whether it's actually the case that the property is not set, especially in light of the %+replace% operation.

NULL indicates that the property inherits from above. When the element properties are calculated with inheritance, all properties must be non-NULL; otherwise it throws an error.

> calc_element('axis.text.x', theme_grey(), verbose = TRUE)
axis.text.x --> axis.text
axis.text --> text
text --> nothing (top level)

List of 8
 $ family    : chr "Helvetica"
 $ face      : chr "plain"

$ colour    : chr "grey50"
 $ size      : num 9.6
 $ hjust     : num 0.5
 $ vjust     : num 1

$ angle     : num 0
 $ lineheight: num 0.9
 - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

> mytheme <- theme_grey() %+replace% theme(text = element_text(colour='red'))
> mytheme$text
List of 8
 $ family    : NULL
 $ face      : NULL
 $ colour    : chr "red"
 $ size      : NULL
 $ hjust     : NULL
 $ vjust     : NULL
 $ angle     : NULL
 $ lineheight: NULL
 - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "element" "element_text"

> calc_element('axis.text.x', mytheme, verbose = TRUE)
axis.text.x --> axis.text
axis.text --> text
text --> Error in FUN("text"[[1L]], ...) :
Theme element 'text' has NULL property: family, face, size, hjust, vjust, angle, lineheight

With the + operator, there's actually no way to set an element property to NULL. (This can be done with the %+replace% operator, though.)

While it may sound a bit limiting to not be able to un-set properties with +, in practice I think it's a good tradeoff for simplicity. Here's an example: in theme_grey, the colour of 'text' is black, but the colour of 'axis.text' is grey50. With the + operator, you can't set axis.text$colour to NULL. You can set it to black, however, and I think that's good enough for most people.

If people want to do fancy stuff like un-setting properties, they can use the %+replace% operator. This would probably be used only by people who are creating their own themes.

-Winston

If I understand correctly the current implementation, setting it explicitly as NULL should do just that:

mytheme = theme_gray() + theme(axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8), angle=45),
                  axis.text.x = element_text(colour="green"),
                  axis.text.y = element_text(colour="red", angle=90))

mytheme + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle=NULL))

doesn't it?

Sorry, this doesn't set mytheme$axis.text.y$angle to NULL.

Implementing this sort of behavior would make other things a lot more complicated. That is -- the behavior when adding an element_text to another element_text should not be defined in the element itself, but by the operator.

For example, suppose you decide to implement something like this: 
theme_grey() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle = NULL))    # No effect
theme_grey() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle = reset_to_NULL))  # Reset angle when added

Then the elements (which are just lists) must be able to carry two different values for $angle: one which means "inherit", and one which means, "when this element is added to another element, reset this property so that it inherits". This is something that is better handled outside the element.


I've updated the wiki page:
https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/New-theme-system

-Winston
